questions.stem: The Indian Wild Ass (Ghudkhur) is the flagship species of a sanctuary in the Little Rann of which state?
questions.explanation: The Indian Wild Ass Sanctuary (Ghudkhur Sanctuary) is located in the Little Rann of Kutch, Gujarat. It is the last refuge of the Indian wild ass (Ghudkhur), the state animal-status species adapted to the saline desert. The sanctuary is also notable for flamingos and other wildlife of the Rann ecosystem.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Gir National Park, the only natural home of the Asiatic lion, is in which state?
questions.explanation: Gir National Park (Gir Forest) in Gujarat is the last natural habitat of the Asiatic lion. Once on the verge of extinction, the lion population has recovered through conservation. Gir is the reason the Asiatic lion survives in the wild only in India.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Which was the first national park established in India (in 1936)?
questions.explanation: Jim Corbett National Park in Uttarakhand, established in 1936 (originally as Hailey National Park), is the oldest national park in India. It was renamed after the hunter-conservationist Jim Corbett. In 1973, it became the first park under Project Tiger.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: 'Project Tiger', launched to conserve the tiger, was started in which year?
questions.explanation: Project Tiger was launched in 1973 by the Government of India to protect the Bengal tiger and its habitats, beginning with Jim Corbett. It is administered by the National Tiger Conservation Authority (NTCA). India now has the largest wild tiger population in the world.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Periyar Wildlife Sanctuary, known for its elephants and located around a lake, is in which state?
questions.explanation: Periyar Wildlife Sanctuary (Periyar Tiger Reserve) in Kerala is set around the Periyar Lake (an artificial reservoir). It is famous for its herds of elephants and boat safaris, and is both a tiger and elephant reserve. It lies in the Western Ghats in Thekkady.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: The Sundarbans National Park, a UNESCO site famous for the Royal Bengal Tiger in mangrove forests, is in which state?
questions.explanation: The Sundarbans National Park in West Bengal lies in the world's largest mangrove delta (Ganga-Brahmaputra), shared with Bangladesh. A UNESCO World Heritage Site and Tiger Reserve, it is famous for the swimming Royal Bengal Tigers adapted to the mangrove ecosystem.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Which national park in Rajasthan is a famous tiger reserve and former hunting ground of the Maharajas of Jaipur?
questions.explanation: Ranthambore National Park in Rajasthan, a renowned tiger reserve, was the former hunting ground of the Maharajas of Jaipur. The historic Ranthambore Fort stands within it. Sariska is another Rajasthan tiger reserve; Keoladeo (Bharatpur) is a bird sanctuary; Desert National Park is in the Thar.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Keoladeo National Park (Bharatpur), a UNESCO World Heritage Site, is famous as a:
questions.explanation: Keoladeo National Park (formerly Bharatpur Bird Sanctuary) in Rajasthan is a famous bird sanctuary and UNESCO World Heritage Site. It was historically a wintering ground for the rare Siberian crane and hosts thousands of migratory birds. It was once a royal duck-hunting reserve.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Which is the largest national park in India by area?
questions.explanation: Hemis National Park in Ladakh is the largest national park in India by area (~4,400 sq km). It is famous as one of the best places in the world to spot the elusive snow leopard, and also hosts the Tibetan wolf and bharal (blue sheep). Its high-altitude cold-desert habitat makes it unique among Indian parks.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Which body is the statutory authority that administers Project Tiger and tiger reserves in India?
questions.explanation: The National Tiger Conservation Authority (NTCA), a statutory body under the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change, administers Project Tiger and oversees tiger reserves. It conducts the periodic tiger census (All India Tiger Estimation). The Wildlife Institute of India is a research/training body.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Which national park, located in Madhya Pradesh, is believed to have inspired Rudyard Kipling's 'The Jungle Book'?
questions.explanation: Kanha National Park in Madhya Pradesh is widely believed to have inspired Rudyard Kipling's 'The Jungle Book'. It is known for its successful conservation of the barasingha (swamp deer). (Pench National Park is also associated with the Jungle Book setting, but Kanha is the most commonly cited inspiration.)
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: 'Project Elephant' was launched by the Government of India in which year?
questions.explanation: Project Elephant was launched in 1992 to protect elephants, their habitats, and migration corridors. India later declared the elephant a National Heritage Animal (2010). Compare: Project Tiger (1973). Both are flagship species-conservation programmes of the Environment Ministry.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Bandipur and Nagarhole National Parks, part of the Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve, are in which state?
questions.explanation: Bandipur and Nagarhole (Rajiv Gandhi) National Parks are in Karnataka, part of the Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve — India's first biosphere reserve. This contiguous forest landscape (with Mudumalai in Tamil Nadu and Wayanad in Kerala) is one of the most important tiger and elephant habitats in southern India.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Which national park in Uttarakhand is a UNESCO World Heritage Site famous for its alpine flowers?
questions.explanation: The Valley of Flowers National Park in Uttarakhand is a UNESCO World Heritage Site renowned for its meadows of endemic alpine flowers and rich biodiversity. It lies in the Western Himalayas near Nanda Devi National Park (together a World Heritage Site) and is home to rare species like the snow leopard and Asiatic black bear.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: The 'Great Indian Bustard', a critically endangered bird, is best associated with the Desert National Park in which state?
questions.explanation: The Great Indian Bustard (state bird of Rajasthan) is critically endangered and is associated with the Desert National Park in Rajasthan (Jaisalmer/Barmer region). Conservation efforts focus on protecting its grassland habitat from threats like power lines. It is one of the heaviest flying birds.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Which state has the highest number of national parks in India?
questions.explanation: The Andaman & Nicobar Islands (a Union Territory) have the highest number of national parks in India (around 9), owing to their many island ecosystems. Among full states, Madhya Pradesh has a high count of large, well-known parks. (Figures can shift with new notifications, so the UT's island parks give it the lead.)
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Simlipal National Park and Biosphere Reserve is located in which state?
questions.explanation: Simlipal National Park (and Tiger Reserve/Biosphere Reserve) is in the Mayurbhanj district of Odisha. It is known for its tigers, elephants, waterfalls, and the rare melanistic (black) tigers reported there. It is part of UNESCO's World Network of Biosphere Reserves.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Which national park, located in Assam, is also famous for the one-horned rhino and is a Tiger Reserve along with Kaziranga?
questions.explanation: Manas National Park in Assam is a UNESCO World Heritage Site, Tiger Reserve, Elephant Reserve, and Biosphere Reserve, located at the foothills of the Himalayas on the India-Bhutan border. It hosts the one-horned rhino and rare species like the pygmy hog and golden langur.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Dachigam National Park, known for the endangered Hangul (Kashmir stag), is in which region?
questions.explanation: Dachigam National Park near Srinagar in Jammu & Kashmir is the last refuge of the Hangul (Kashmir stag), the state animal of J&K and the only species of red deer found in India. The park's name means 'ten villages' (relocated to create it).
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Which national park in India was the location where cheetahs were reintroduced in 2022 under 'Project Cheetah'?
questions.explanation: Kuno National Park in Madhya Pradesh was the site of the reintroduction of cheetahs in September 2022 under 'Project Cheetah', bringing African cheetahs from Namibia and South Africa. The cheetah had been declared extinct in India in 1952, making this the world's first intercontinental large-carnivore translocation.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: What is the key difference between a National Park and a Wildlife Sanctuary in India?

options.text: A National Park has stricter protection (no human activity/grazing allowed and boundaries fixed by legislation), whereas a Wildlife Sanctuary permits certain regulated human activities and has more flexible boundaries
There is no legal difference between them
A Wildlife Sanctuary protects only birds; a National Park protects only mammals
A National Park is privately owned; a Wildlife Sanctuary is government-owned

questions.explanation: Under the Wildlife Protection Act, 1972: a National Park has stricter protection — no human activity, grazing, or private land rights are allowed, and its boundaries are well-defined. A Wildlife Sanctuary allows certain regulated human activities (like grazing or collection of minor forest produce with permission) and can be altered more easily. A national park can be created from a sanctuary, but not the reverse without due process.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: The 'Silent Valley National Park', the site of a famous environmental movement against a hydroelectric project, is in which state?
questions.explanation: Silent Valley National Park in Kerala (Palakkad district) was the focus of the Silent Valley Movement (late 1970s–80s), a landmark environmental campaign that successfully stopped a proposed hydroelectric dam on the Kunthipuzha river to save the pristine tropical rainforest, home to the lion-tailed macaque. It was declared a national park in 1984.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Namdapha National Park, the largest protected area in the Eastern Himalayas and notable for hosting four big cat species, is in which state?
questions.explanation: Namdapha National Park in Arunachal Pradesh is the largest protected area in the Eastern Himalayas and is unique for hosting four big cat species — tiger, leopard, snow leopard, and clouded leopard. Its vast altitudinal range (200 m to 4,500 m) gives it exceptional biodiversity.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Which of the following is India's first marine national park?

options.text: Gulf of Mannar Marine National Park
Marine National Park, Gulf of Kutch

questions.explanation: The Marine National Park in the Gulf of Kutch, Gujarat, established in 1982, was India's first marine national park. It protects coral reefs, mangroves, and diverse marine life. The Gulf of Mannar (Tamil Nadu) is India's first Marine Biosphere Reserve, a related but distinct designation.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: The 'biosphere reserve' designation differs from a national park in that a biosphere reserve:

options.text: Is smaller than a national park
Is a larger, zoned conservation area (core, buffer, transition) that integrates biodiversity protection with sustainable human use, and may contain national parks/sanctuaries within it
Protects only a single endangered species

questions.explanation: A biosphere reserve is a large, internationally recognised (UNESCO MAB programme) conservation area organised into zones: a strictly protected CORE zone, a BUFFER zone for limited research/activity, and a TRANSITION zone for sustainable human use. It is bigger than a national park and often contains national parks/sanctuaries within its core. India's first was the Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve (1986).
questions.subject: General Knowledge
